title: Existence of boundary germ lifts in depth two
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, $j:U\hookrightarrow L$, and $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] finite on every affine open. Suppose every $N_y$ for $y\notin U$ is finite and has depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Assume the restriction unit $N(V)\to (j_*(N|_U))(V)$ is injective on every open $V$. Then for every $y\notin U$ its stalk map $N_y\to (j_*(N|_U))_y$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0E9I, surjectivity argument of Tag 0AV8; Tags 0AVN, 05AM, 00LL and 00LX

proof.text: Represent the target germ by a section s over an affine neighbourhood V, using Mathlib exists_mem_germ_eq_of_isBasis and Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens. Put a for the section unit and S = range(a) + R s. Its finite generation follows from finiteness of the source and the singleton span. Let K be range(a) pulled back to S and Q = S/K.

Apply the positive local depth theorem for the finite intermediate quotient Q. If Q were nonzero, Mathlib associatedPrimes.nonempty supplies an associated prime p. The associated prime localization theorem makes the maximal ideal associated to Q_p. Nakayama ensures m Q_p is not Q_p. In the regular-sequence definition of depth, any nonempty regular sequence in m would start with an element both regular and in the union of associated primes, a contradiction. Thus depth(Q_p)=0, contradicting its lower bound one. This is the proved private helper subsingleton_of_positive_local_depth.

The quotient is subsingleton, so the class of s in Q is zero. The quotient zero criterion puts s in range(a); choose its preimage r. The naturality identity stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply identifies the image of the germ of r with the germ of s, which is the chosen target germ.

    (hdepth : ∀ y : L, y ∉ U →

        letI := hfinite
        (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := L.presheaf.stalk y)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := L) N.val.presheaf y)) 
    (hinj : ∀ V : L.Opens,
      Function.Injective (((Modules.restrictAdjunction U.ι).unit.app N).app V))
    (y : L) (hy : y ∉ U) :
